decisions.decision: TASK-024 JOIN window semantics [ASSUMED] (resolves rev-t024 MEDIUM-1): once >=2 players are ready, JOIN stays OPEN for the remainder of its 30 s window and exits early ONLY when all 4 seats are claimed; it never instant-exits on the 2nd claim. Rationale: GDD 2.1's '>=2 jugadores listos' label is ambiguous between condition-fires and minimum-met; GDD 9.3's timeline budgets up to 30 s for color choice; the social premise makes locking out seats 3/4 the worst reading; all-4-claimed early exit invents no constants (nobody is left to join). Cost accepted: 2-3-player groups wait out the window — a future 'start now' gesture may shorten it (candidate item for TASK-028 UAT or the board UX ticket). [ASSUMED]-tagged + test-pinned; human may veto.
decisions.rationale: Fixes the seat-3/4 lockout with zero invented constants, staying inside GDD-stated numbers; the alternative grace-window designs all invent an unstated duration.

decisions.decision: Bookkeeping-durability ground rules after the ~13:20Z incident (RECORD CORRECTION 14:20Z: dev-t101 used git stash push -u — NON-destructive, single stash@{0}, second attempt was a no-op after acf7605; nothing was actually destroyed, but the effect on the working tree was identical: all tasks/session writes after chore commit 2c1bc38 vanished from disk and the untracked TASK-049/050/051 files with them; everything re-applied from conversation context before the stash was discovered, comments marked [RE-APPLIED], tickets re-minted with identical keys; stash@{0} kept for the human's .claude/settings.json restore + Editor-noise discard decision): (1) the orchestrator COMMITS ticket/bundle bookkeeping immediately after writing it whenever any developer shares the live working tree — uncommitted state may not survive a teammate's git operations; (2) developers/agents NEVER clean, checkout, stash-drop, or git-clean tasks/, state/, or untracked files — if orchestrator-owned files block a git operation, pause and ping the orchestrator; (3) cherry-pick conflict resolution on tasks/ files is always --ours (local task store wins; the orchestrator merges any cloud ticket notes manually).
decisions.rationale: The shared-working-tree model (one writer on master = the main checkout) makes uncommitted orchestrator files casualties of any dev tree-hygiene step; committing immediately is the only durable protection, and the no-clean rule plus --ours convention prevent recurrence. No code or review evidence was lost — only bookkeeping, all reconstructable this time because the session context still held every write.
